beats.say: The churn model scored ninety nine percent in the notebook. In production, seventy.
beats.label: The problem
beats.head: 99% in the notebook, 70% in production

beats.say: The exam loves this story. Today you learn why it happens, and how to fix it.
beats.label: Station 4.4 · ML fundamentals
beats.head: Why it happens, and the fix

check.prompt: You forecast sales from three years of data. How do you split it?
options: By time: past to train, recent to test
No split, use all of it
check.why: A random split lets the model see the future.

beats.say: First, split your data three ways. Each part has one job.
Training teaches the weights. Validation picks the settings. The test set gives the honest score, once.
beats.label: Split the data

beats.say: For time series, split by time. A random split lets the model see the future.
beats.label: Time series
beats.head: Train on the past, test on the future

beats.say: And watch for leakage: a feature you only know after the outcome.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: A feature known only after the outcome

beats.say: Now compare two scores: training and validation.
High on training, low on validation, is overfitting. The model memorized the rows.
beats.label: Overfitting
beats.head: Great on training, poor on new data

beats.say: Low on both is underfitting. The model is too simple. Give it more features or more power.
beats.label: Underfitting
beats.head: Poor on both: too simple

check.prompt: A deep network with many layers fits training data but fails on new data. The fix?
check.why: Dropout stops a big network from memorizing. Threading and serialization only change speed and storage.

beats.say: Four tools stop a model from memorizing.
Dropout. During training, it switches off random neurons at every step.
beats.label: Dropout
beats.head: Random neurons off, every training step

beats.say: No neuron can lean on another, so the network learns general patterns. At prediction, all neurons are on.
beats.label: Why it works
beats.head: No neuron can lean on another

beats.say: L one pushes weak features to zero. L two keeps every weight small. Early stopping ends at the best epoch.
beats.label: The other three
items: L1: weak features go to zero

beats.say: The trap: more layers or more epochs. They make overfitting worse.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: More layers, more epochs: worse overfitting

check.prompt: Fraud is one in a thousand. Which metric should you watch?
check.why: Saying never fraud is 99.9% accurate and catches nothing.

beats.say: Next, pick the metric that matches the cost of a mistake.
beats.text: Match the cost of a mistake

beats.say: If a miss is costly, like a disease, use recall. If a false alarm is costly, use precision.
beats.label: Classification
items: A false alarm is costly: precision

beats.say: Lower the threshold for more recall. Raise it for more precision. No retraining.
beats.label: The threshold
beats.head: Move the threshold, not the model

beats.say: With rare cases, like fraud, accuracy lies. Use PR AUC.
beats.label: Rare positives
beats.head: Accuracy lies. Use PR AUC.

beats.say: Last, features. They matter more than the algorithm.
Scale your numbers. One hot small categories. Embed huge ones.
beats.label: The toolkit

beats.say: And cross features that work together, like latitude and longitude.
beats.label: Feature cross
beats.head: Latitude × longitude = a place

beats.say: Put these steps in the transform clause, so prediction repeats them exactly.
beats.label: BigQuery ML
beats.head: Keep them in TRANSFORM

beats.say: Recap.
Split honestly. Read the gap. Dropout for big networks. Pick the metric by the cost of a mistake.
beats.label: Station 4.4
items: Metric by cost of a mistake
